question: Of the following complex numbers \(z,\) which one has the property that \(z^5\) has the greatest real part?
solution:
All five choices have modulus \(2\), so polar form makes their fifth powers easy to compare. Write
\[
z=2(\cos\theta+i\sin\theta).
\]
By De Moivre's formula,
\[
z^5=32(\cos5\theta+i\sin5\theta),
\]
whose real part is \(32\cos5\theta\). Reducing the angles by multiples of \(2\pi\) gives
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
\text{Choice}&\theta&5\theta\text{ reduced}&\operatorname{Re}(z^5)\\ \hline
\text{A}&\pi&5\pi-4\pi=\pi&-32\\
\text{B}&\frac{5\pi}{6}&\frac{25\pi}{6}-4\pi=\frac{\pi}{6}&16\sqrt3\\
\text{C}&\frac{3\pi}{4}&\frac{15\pi}{4}-4\pi=-\frac{\pi}{4}&16\sqrt2\\
\text{D}&\frac{2\pi}{3}&\frac{10\pi}{3}-4\pi=-\frac{2\pi}{3}&-16\\
\text{E}&\frac{\pi}{2}&\frac{5\pi}{2}-2\pi=\frac{\pi}{2}&0
\end{array}
\]
Since \(16\sqrt3>16\sqrt2>0\), the greatest real part occurs for \(\boxed{z=-\sqrt3+i}\), choice \(\text{B}\).
